summary: Explains where to find the latest ansible.cfg (in `/etc/ansible`, possibly as `.rpmnew`, for package installs) and that pip or source installs may need one created. Shows generating a full commented config with `ansible-config init --disabled`, adding `-t all` for plugin settings.
questions: Why is there no ansible.cfg after installing Ansible with pip?
How do I generate an ansible.cfg with all the default settings?
How do I include plugin options in a generated ansible.cfg?
Where is the default ansible.cfg on a package-manager install?
Why do I have an ansible.cfg.rpmnew file?
How can I see my current Ansible configuration values?

answer_card.title: Generate an ansible.cfg
answer_card.answer_md:
Package-manager installs put the latest `ansible.cfg` in `/etc/ansible` (after updates it may appear as `.rpmnew` or similar). pip or source installs don't create one; create it yourself to override defaults.

Generate a file listing all defaults (commented out):
```console
$ ansible-config init --disabled > ansible.cfg
```
Include available plugins too:
```console
$ ansible-config init --disabled -t all > ansible.cfg
```
Use the `ansible-config` utility to list options and inspect current values.
